overview: The capacity methods report what the pools a tenant can see hold, book and have free, without booking anything. `summary` and `byPool` read the per-pool rollup, which the booking transactions update and a periodic rebuild corrects. `preview` asks the placer whether a request fits, and `timeline` counts booked GPUs over time. All four are decided as `compute:capacity:read`. See [Capacity](/docs/guides/capacity).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns every pool the tenant owns or is offered, each with its rollup rows, plus whole-GPU totals per GPU model.
methods.description:
Returns every pool the tenant owns or is offered, each with its rollup rows, plus whole-GPU totals per GPU model.

Archived pools appear only for their owner. `byGpuModel` sums only each pool's `gpu` row (`total`, `allocatable`, `allocated`, `reserved`, `available`), and a pool without a GPU model is counted under `other`. The `gpu.mig`, `gpu.slot` and scalar rows are in `pools[].capacity`. The decision is made on the tenant.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns one pool's rollup rows, one per resource, ordered by resource name.
methods.description:
Returns one pool's rollup rows, one per resource, ordered by resource name.

Each row carries `total`, `allocatable`, `allocated`, `reserved`, `available`, the `provisioning`, `unhealthy`, `maintenance` and `unreachable` buckets, and `updatedAt`. `available` is conservative: an atom booked now and again later counts in both `allocated` and `reserved`. The call is `NOT_FOUND` when the pool is not owned by or offered to the tenant, or is archived and the tenant is not its owner. `pools.capacity` returns the same rows.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

selector.description: matchExpressions over device attributes, then node labels

binding.description: hold (CDI devices), node (a whole-node lease in a tenantRoot pool) or kubernetes (the devices advertised to the node’s kubelet, in a pool with policy.kubernetes)

idempotencyKey.description: Scoped to (tenant, caller identity): a retry with the same key replays

methods.summary: Runs the placer on a reservation request without booking anything and returns whether it fits now, the candidate nodes with the atoms each would take, and a reason when it does not fit.
methods.description:
Runs the placer on a reservation request without booking anything and returns whether it fits now, the candidate nodes with the atoms each would take, and a reason when it does not fit.

- The input is the `reservations.create` input, validated the same way, `idempotencyKey` included. Nothing is written and no quota is checked.
- Up to 10 ranked candidates are returned, each with `nodeId`, `atoms` and `score`. With `gang`, the candidates are the members of the best gang. With `binding: 'node'`, they are the whole nodes a lease would take.
- When a regular (not `spot`) request does not fit, `preemptible` says how many spot reservations would get a notice and when the request would start. It gives a count only, never the other reservations' ids.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the pool is not visible to the tenant.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns, for one pool, the number of whole GPUs booked in each time bucket and how many of the pool's allocatable GPUs remain free.
methods.description:
Returns, for one pool, the number of whole GPUs booked in each time bucket and how many of the pool's allocatable GPUs remain free.

`from` defaults to the start of the current hour, `to` to 24 hours after `from`, and `stepMinutes` to 60. A timeline spans at most 7 days and 336 buckets, and `to` must be after `from`; otherwise the call is `INVALID_INPUT`. `allocatable` comes from the pool's current `gpu` rollup row, and each bucket's `free` is `allocatable` minus `booked`, never below 0. MIG and slot atoms are not counted. `NOT_FOUND` when the pool is not visible to the tenant.

overview: Destructive-command batches (v1.0 quorum). A batch fixes a set of (subject, kind) leaves, optionally bound to exact payloads, under one Merkle root when it is created (modules create them through `commands.createBatch`). When the deployment publishes approver keys (`pki.approvers`), the batch's commands wait until enough approvers, holding keys off the control plane, have signed its root for the trust domain. The gateway then sends each command with the approval and its leaf's proof, and the daemon verifies both. Without approver keys a batch is recorded for audit and its commands go out at once. See [Security](/docs/operations/security).

methods.summary: Creates a batch from its (subject, kind) leaves, each optionally bound to a payload's SHA-256, a reason and a lifetime; returns it `pending`, with the approvals its size needs.
methods.description:
Creates a batch from its (subject, kind) leaves, each optionally bound to a payload's SHA-256, a reason and a lifetime; returns it `pending`, with the approvals its size needs.

- The tree is fixed now: its root, size and every leaf's proof are stored, so what approvers review is what the daemons check. Subjects are computed as the executing agent does (see pki `batchSubject`): the node id, `bmc:<site agent>/<address>` for BMC kinds, `node:<target>` for `site.httpProxy`. A leaf without `payloadSha256` admits any payload of its kind, and `scope` flags it to approvers.
- **Idempotency.** The batch id derives from the tenant, the caller and `idempotencyKey`. The same request again (the same leaves in any order, reason and lifetime) returns the stored batch without a new event; a different request under the key is `CONFLICT`.
- The lifetime is `notAfterSeconds` (default 24 hours): after it the batch admits no commands and can no longer be approved. At most 50,000 leaves.

Publishes `command.batch.created` with the scope size and the approvals required.

methods.summary: Returns one batch of the tenant: its reason, state, scope root and size, the approvals it needs and has, and how many of its commands are in each state.
methods.description:
Returns one batch of the tenant: its reason, state, scope root and size, the approvals it needs and has, and how many of its commands are in each state.

The state is `expired` as soon as `notAfter` passes, even before the minute sweep writes it. A batch of another tenant is `NOT_FOUND`.

`createdBy` is the identity that created the batch. When an agent proposed it on that identity's behalf (MCP `propose_command_batch`), `createdByAgent` and `delegationId` say so, and the `reason` is the agent's text, not the person's.

methods.summary: Returns the tenant's batches, newest first, filtered by `state`.
methods.description:
Returns the tenant's batches, newest first, filtered by `state`.

`limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50); `next`, when present, is the `cursor` for the following page.

methods.summary: Returns a batch's leaves in leaf order, for approvers to review before signing: each leaf's index, subject, kind and `payloadSha256`, plus the leaf's `payload` (`{ typeUrl, value }` base64) when its creator stored it. Decode it by the kind's payload type, after checking it against `payloadSha256`.
methods.description:
Returns a batch's leaves in leaf order, for approvers to review before signing: each leaf's index, subject, kind and `payloadSha256`, plus the leaf's `payload` (`{ typeUrl, value }` base64) when its creator stored it. Decode it by the kind's payload type, after checking it against `payloadSha256`.

An empty `payloadSha256` marks a leaf that admits any payload of its kind, which approvers should look at closely. Pages hold 1 to 5,000 leaves (1,000 by default); `next` is the leaf index to pass as `cursor`.

methods.summary: Returns the commands enqueued into a batch so far, in command-id order: each one's node, (subject, kind), state and reason, and `awaitingApproval` while it is held for the batch's approval.
methods.description:
Returns the commands enqueued into a batch so far, in command-id order: each one's node, (subject, kind), state and reason, and `awaitingApproval` while it is held for the batch's approval.

`state` keeps one command state. Pages hold 1 to 500 commands (100 by default); `next` is the command id to pass as `cursor`. A batch of another tenant is `NOT_FOUND`.

methods.summary: Adds one approver's signature over the batch's root; once the signatures meet the threshold for its size, the batch becomes `approved` and its held commands are released at once.
methods.description:
Adds one approver's signature over the batch's root; once the signatures meet the threshold for its size, the batch becomes `approved` and its held commands are released at once.

- `signature` is `{ kid, sig }`: the approver key id and a base64url P-256 signature over the batch (id, root, size, end, trust domain), made off the control plane. A signature by a key outside the published set, or over anything else, is `ACCESS_DENIED`. The same approver twice counts once.
- Decided as `compute:batches:approve`, on top of the signature, never instead of it.
- `INVALID_STATE` for a batch that is not `pending`, or one that needs no approvals (no approver keys, or a size the tiers exempt). `INVALID_CONFIG` when the deployment has no trust domain (no `pki.join`).

Publishes `command.batch.approved` with the approver key ids when the batch completes.

methods.summary: Ends a pending batch: it becomes `cancelled` and its held commands are cancelled with it.
methods.description:
Ends a pending batch: it becomes `cancelled` and its held commands are cancelled with it.

A batch that is not `pending` is `INVALID_STATE`. Decided as `compute:batches:approve`.

overview: One-shot actions on one node, queued as durable rows in the node's command queue and delivered in order over its session. Every method is decided on `compute-node/{nodeId}`: `run` and `cancel` with `compute:nodes:exec`, `get` and `list` with `compute:nodes:read`. See [Commands](/docs/guides/nodes/commands).

methods.summary: Queues a command of an allowlisted kind (`diag.nvml`, `inventory.refresh`, `logs.collect`, `node.reboot`) on a node the tenant can see; returns the command, `pending` when first queued.
methods.description:
Queues a command of an allowlisted kind (`diag.nvml`, `inventory.refresh`, `logs.collect`, `node.reboot`) on a node the tenant can see; returns the command, `pending` when first queued.

- Idempotent per tenant, caller identity and `idempotencyKey`: a retry with the same key returns the command already queued. The same key with a different `kind` is `CONFLICT`.
- `notAfterSeconds` (10 to 3600, default 600) sets how long the command may wait for the node before it expires.
- Any other kind is `UNSUPPORTED`; a payload that does not match the kind's schema is `INVALID_INPUT`; a node outside the tenant's view is `NOT_FOUND`.
- For `logs.collect`, when the server has `supportBundles` with a presigning blob store, the daemon receives a presigned upload URL and the response carries the bundle's `bundleKey`.
- Emits `node.command.queued` when the command is first queued, not on a replay.

methods.summary: Returns one command of a node by id, with its state, deadlines and safety flags.
methods.description:
Returns one command of a node by id, with its state, deadlines and safety flags.

`NOT_FOUND` when the command is not on that node or the node is outside the tenant's view.

methods.summary: Lists a node's commands newest first (by queue sequence), optionally filtered by `state`; returns a page with a cursor.
methods.description:
Lists a node's commands newest first (by queue sequence), optionally filtered by `state`; returns a page with a cursor.

`limit` is at most 200 (100 by default). The cursor is the sequence of the last command returned.

methods.summary: Cancels a command: a `pending` one becomes `cancelled` and never runs, an in-flight one (`dispatched`, `acked`, `running`) is asked to stop through its gateway; returns the command as it stands after the request.
methods.description:
Cancels a command: a `pending` one becomes `cancelled` and never runs, an in-flight one (`dispatched`, `acked`, `running`) is asked to stop through its gateway; returns the command as it stands after the request.

- A command already in a terminal state (`succeeded`, `failed`, `rejected`, `expired`, `cancelled`) is returned unchanged and no event is emitted.
- An in-flight command keeps its state until the node reports; the request is recorded on the row.
- Emits `node.command.cancel-requested`. `NOT_FOUND` when the command is not on that node or the node is outside the tenant's view.

overview: The drivers this deployment registered through its options, modules and plugins, so `metal.enroll` callers and the console can offer valid choices. The group returns declarations only, never a driver's configuration or credentials. See [Drivers](/docs/extending/drivers).

methods.summary: Lists the registered drivers with their id, version, `runsOn`, implemented kinds, capabilities and the operations safe to retry per kind; `kind` keeps only drivers that implement it.
methods.description:
Lists the registered drivers with their id, version, `runsOn`, implemented kinds, capabilities and the operations safe to retry per kind; `kind` keeps only drivers that implement it.

Decided with `compute:drivers:read` on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`. Items are sorted by id, then version, and the result is not paged.

overview: A tenant's CloudEvents-style events, read from the transactional outbox that every change writes to in its own transaction. Pages follow the outbox's `txid:seq` position, so no event ever appears behind a cursor already handed out. See [Events](/docs/guides/events).

methods.summary: Returns a page of the tenant's committed events after `cursor`, oldest first, optionally only those whose type starts with `type` (for example `node.` or `reservation.`).
methods.description:
Returns a page of the tenant's committed events after `cursor`, oldest first, optionally only those whose type starts with `type` (for example `node.` or `reservation.`).

- Decided with `compute:events:read` on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`.
- The cursor is an event's `sequence` in the form `txid:seq`; without one the page starts at the oldest event still in the outbox.
- Only events whose transaction is older than every transaction still open are returned, so a later page never gains an event that sorts before its cursor.
- `limit` is at most 500 (100 by default).

overview: Flavors are the named instance shapes of a VPS pool: vCPU, memory, disk and GPU count, plus the provider offer a provider pool creates. The pool's owner manages them, and tenants the pool is offered to can list them. An instance keeps the shape it was admitted with, so changing or deleting a flavor never changes a live instance. See [Flavors](/docs/guides/vps/flavors).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns the pool's flavors that are not archived, sorted by name.
methods.description:
Returns the pool's flavors that are not archived, sorted by name.

The pool must be owned by or offered to the tenant; otherwise the call is `NOT_FOUND`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

offerId.description: Provider pools: the provider offer this flavor creates (required there)

numaAffine.description: vCPUs and memory on one NUMA node (its GPUs’ node when it has any)

pinned.description: Each vCPU on its own host CPU

hugepages.description: Back guest memory with hugepages of this size (books the host’s hugepages)

placement.description: Hosted pools (v1.1): where the guest lives on its host; sandbox templates inherit it

methods.summary: Adds a flavor to a `vps-host` or `provider` pool the tenant owns and returns it at version 1.
methods.description:
Adds a flavor to a `vps-host` or `provider` pool the tenant owns and returns it at version 1.

- `gpus` defaults to 0. A flavor of a provider pool needs `offerId`, the provider offer it creates; without it the call is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- `placement` (hosted pools only; `INVALID_INPUT` on a provider pool) says where the guest lives on its host, and sandbox templates on the flavor inherit it:
  - `hugepages: '2Mi' | '1Gi'` backs guest memory with hugepages. These are booked from the host's hugepage pools instead of its memory, still charged to quota as `memoryGiB`, and never ballooned.
  - `numaAffine` keeps the vCPUs and memory on one NUMA node: the GPUs' node, or otherwise the least-loaded node with room for the memory.
  - `pinned` gives each vCPU a host CPU that no other pinned guest on the host has.
  - A host that cannot honour `numaAffine` or `pinned` still runs the guest, floating, and the instance carries a `PlacementDegraded` condition with the reason (`NoNumaTopology`, `NoNumaNodeFits`, `GpuNumaUnknown`, `NumaMemoryTooSmall` or `NotEnoughFreeCpus`).
  - Resizing to a flavor with a different `placement` is `UNSUPPORTED`.
- In a pool that overcommits memory (`policy.overcommit.memoryGiB` > 1), every guest gets a virtio balloon so the host can reclaim its free memory. The exceptions are hugepage-backed guests and guests with GPUs, whose memory is pinned. This needs no flavor field.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the tenant does not own the pool; `INVALID_STATE` when the pool is of another class.
- `CONFLICT` when the pool already has a flavor with that name, archived ones included.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

offerId.description: Provider pools: the provider offer this flavor creates (required there)

numaAffine.description: vCPUs and memory on one NUMA node (its GPUs’ node when it has any)

pinned.description: Each vCPU on its own host CPU

hugepages.description: Back guest memory with hugepages of this size (books the host’s hugepages)

placement.description: Hosted pools (v1.1): where the guest lives on its host; sandbox templates inherit it

methods.summary: Replaces the shape of the named flavor and increments its version; an archived flavor becomes active again.
methods.description:
Replaces the shape of the named flavor and increments its version; an archived flavor becomes active again.

The input is the full shape, as for `create`. An omitted `offerId` keeps the stored one. Instances already admitted keep their old shape; only new instances and resizes use the new one. The call is `NOT_FOUND` when the tenant does not own the pool or the flavor does not exist.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Deletes the named flavor, or archives it when any instance, deleted ones included, still references it; returns `deleted` and `archived` to say which.
methods.description:
Deletes the named flavor, or archives it when any instance, deleted ones included, still references it; returns `deleted` and `archived` to say which.

An archived flavor disappears from `list` and can no longer be used to create or resize instances. `update` makes it active again. The call is `NOT_FOUND` when the tenant does not own the pool or the flavor does not exist.

overview: The fleet group manages a tenant's platform objects as one FleetConfig document: sites, provider accounts, pools, owner quotas, offers and flavors. `plan` diffs a document against what exists, `apply` runs the plan through the owning modules' own methods, and the applied document is kept so that drift from it is reported. Every method decides `compute:fleet:admin` on the fleet scope. See [Fleet configuration](/docs/guides/fleet-config).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns the tenant's current sites, provider accounts, pools, owner quotas, offers and flavors as a FleetConfig document, with `missing` listing the tables of modules this deployment does not run.
methods.description:
Returns the tenant's current sites, provider accounts, pools, owner quotas, offers and flavors as a FleetConfig document, with `missing` listing the tables of modules this deployment does not run.

Objects that fleet never named appear under their ids. Archived pools and archived flavors are left out.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

config.description: The FleetConfig document: { version: 1, sites, providerAccounts, pools, flavors, sandboxTemplates }, as fleet.export writes it

prune.description: Delete (archive) what the document no longer lists

methods.summary: Diffs a FleetConfig document against the tenant's current state; returns the changes for people, the exact API calls `apply` would make, a summary, `blocked`, and a `planHash`.
methods.description:
Diffs a FleetConfig document against the tenant's current state; returns the changes for people, the exact API calls `apply` would make, a summary, `blocked`, and a `planHash`.

- The call changes nothing. With `prune: true` the plan also deletes what the document no longer lists: flavors and offers are removed, pools archived, and unused provider accounts deleted. Sites are never changed or pruned.
- A change that cannot be applied (an immutable field such as a pool's class or an account's provider, an unknown reference, an offer to the pool's owner) is marked `blocked` with the reason.
- The ids of planned creates derive from the caller's identity, so the call needs an authenticated caller (`UNAUTHENTICATED` otherwise).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

config.description: The FleetConfig document: { version: 1, sites, providerAccounts, pools, flavors, sandboxTemplates }, as fleet.export writes it

prune.description: Delete (archive) what the document no longer lists

planHash.description: The planHash of the plan you reviewed: apply refuses with CONFIG_DRIFT if the plan moved since

methods.summary: Plans the document again and runs every planned call as the caller, all in one transaction; returns the plan and the number of calls applied.
methods.description:
Plans the document again and runs every planned call as the caller, all in one transaction; returns the plan and the number of calls applied.

- **Decisions.** Each call is authorized first, as the caller and with no transaction open, by the method it invokes; a refusal stops the apply before anything changes.
- **Consistency.** Pass the `planHash` from `plan` to apply exactly that plan: if the plan has changed, the call is `CONFIG_DRIFT`. The plan is made once more inside the transaction, and a change there is also `CONFIG_DRIFT`, with nothing applied.
- **Idempotency.** Creates carry keys derived from the tenant, the kind and the name, so repeating an apply creates nothing twice. A plan with no calls still records the document.
- **Errors.** `INVALID_STATE` with `details.blocked` when any change is blocked. `UNSUPPORTED` when the host cannot run composite methods. Errors of the invoked methods pass through.
- The document becomes the one that `status` and the `fleet.drift` reconciler compare against.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns the tenant's last applied document's plan hash, who applied it and when, and, while the fleet differs from it, the drift found at the last check.
methods.description:
Returns the tenant's last applied document's plan hash, who applied it and when, and, while the fleet differs from it, the drift found at the last check.

`applied` is absent when the tenant never applied a document. The `fleet.drift` reconciler re-plans each applied document every 15 minutes by default and publishes `fleet.drifted` or `fleet.converged` when the answer changes.

overview: The images group is the catalog of OS images and ramdisks that deploys write to disk. An image is registered by its digest and source URL, never uploaded, and a signature from a signer on the tenant's or the platform's allowlist marks it verified. Unsigned images stay private to their tenant; only verified images can be made public. See [Profiles and images](/docs/guides/bare-metal/profiles-and-images).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

sha256.description: The digest of the image, 64 hex digits

source.description: Where the image is fetched from: an https:// or oci:// URL

signature.description: Base64 signature over the image's identity (kind, ref, format, compression, sha256)

signerId.description: The registered signer whose key checks the signature

methods.summary: Records an image by `ref` (`name@version`), format, digest and `https://` or `oci://` source in the tenant's catalog; with a valid signature it is marked verified.
methods.description:
Records an image by `ref` (`name@version`), format, digest and `https://` or `oci://` source in the tenant's catalog; with a valid signature it is marked verified.

- Decided as `compute:images:publish` on the tenant.
- `signature` and `signerId` go together. The signature must verify against that signer on the tenant's allowlist or the platform's, else `INVALID_INPUT`.
- A `ramdisk` must be signed by a platform signer (`INVALID_INPUT` otherwise).
- `CONFLICT` when the tenant already has that `ref`, so a repeated call does not create a second image.

The new image is private. Site agents whose pools pre-warm this ref (`policy.prewarmImages`) get their desired state refreshed.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns one image the tenant owns, or a public one, by its `img_` id.
methods.description:
Returns one image the tenant owns, or a public one, by its `img_` id.

`NOT_FOUND` when the image does not exist, is deleted, or belongs to another tenant and is not public.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

cursor.description: The cursor of the previous page

methods.summary: Returns a page of the tenant's own images and public ones, ordered by `ref`, optionally filtered by `kind` (`os` or `ramdisk`).
methods.description:
Returns a page of the tenant's own images and public ones, ordered by `ref`, optionally filtered by `kind` (`os` or `ramdisk`).

`limit` defaults to 50 and is at most 200; pass the returned `cursor` to read the next page.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Makes a verified image the tenant owns public, so every tenant can read and deploy it.
methods.description:
Makes a verified image the tenant owns public, so every tenant can read and deploy it.

Decided as `compute:images:publish` on the image. An unsigned image is `INVALID_STATE`; an image the tenant does not own is `NOT_FOUND`. Promoting an image that is already public returns it unchanged. Site agents whose pools pre-warm this ref get their desired state refreshed.

overview: Instances are VMs in a VPS pool: hosted pools place them on a host through capacity, and provider pools create them through the pool's provider account. After `create`, every call only changes `desiredState`; the `vps.instances` reconciler converges the instance and publishes `instance.*` events as its `state` moves. Instances are also the sandbox primitive today. See [Instances](/docs/guides/vps/instances).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

sshKeys.description: OpenSSH public keys, one line each

userData.description: User data (at most 32 KiB), or secret://<tenantId>/<id> naming a secret of this tenant

idempotencyKey.description: Scoped to (tenant, caller identity): a retry with the same key replays

timeoutMs.description: How long to hold the answer until the instance settles

methods.summary: Admits a VM from a pool, flavor and image after one IAM decision on the draft; returns the instance in `scheduling`, or in `provisioning` with a `nodeId` when a hosted pool placed it at once.
methods.description:
Admits a VM from a pool, flavor and image after one IAM decision on the draft; returns the instance in `scheduling`, or in `provisioning` with a `nodeId` when a hosted pool placed it at once.

- **Idempotency.** `idempotencyKey` is required. The instance id derives from the tenant, the caller and the key: a retry of a finished request returns the same instance without a second decision, and a different request under the same key is `CONFLICT` with `details.instanceId`.
- **IAM.** `compute:instances:create` is decided on `compute-instance/` plus the draft id, whose attributes (`vcpu`, `memoryGiB`, `gpus`, `imageId`, `imageVerified`, `projectId`) policies can test. A refusal deletes the draft; a delegated session can get `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`.
- **Errors.** `NOT_FOUND` for a pool the tenant neither owns nor is offered, an archived pool, a missing or archived flavor, or an image a hosted pool cannot resolve. `INVALID_INPUT` for a pool that is not `vps-host` or `provider`. `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` when the shape does not fit the tenant's quota; `CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE` when a hosted pool has no free IP address. `INVALID_STATE` for a provider pool without an account, `INVALID_CONFIG` for a hosted pool when `vps()` has no `images`.
- **Events.** `instance.created`, and `instance.scheduled` with the `nodeId` when a hosted instance is placed. When no host fits, the instance stays in `scheduling` with an `Unschedulable` condition and is retried every 30 seconds.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

cursor.description: The last instance id of the previous page

methods.summary: Returns a page of the tenant's instances, newest first, with a `cursor` when more remain.
methods.description:
Returns a page of the tenant's instances, newest first, with a `cursor` when more remain.

`scope` defaults to `mine`, the caller's own instances; `all` returns every instance of the tenant that the caller may read. `state` and `poolId` filter the list, and `limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50). Drafts are never listed.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns one instance of the tenant, deleted instances included.
methods.description:
Returns one instance of the tenant, deleted instances included.

Drafts and instances of other tenants are `NOT_FOUND`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Sets `desiredState` to `running` and wakes the reconciler; returns the instance before anything has changed on the host or provider.
methods.description:
Sets `desiredState` to `running` and wakes the reconciler; returns the instance before anything has changed on the host or provider.

An instance in `error` that has a host or a provider machine moves to `starting` and is tried again. An instance being deleted is `INVALID_STATE`. Publishes `instance.starting`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Sets `desiredState` to `stopped` and wakes the reconciler; returns the instance before anything has changed on the host or provider.
methods.description:
Sets `desiredState` to `stopped` and wakes the reconciler; returns the instance before anything has changed on the host or provider.

An instance being deleted is `INVALID_STATE`. Publishes `instance.stopping`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a stopped hosted instance to another flavor of its pool, in place on the same host; returns the instance `stopped` with the new flavor.
methods.description:
Moves a stopped hosted instance to another flavor of its pool, in place on the same host; returns the instance `stopped` with the new flavor.

Growth is charged to quota first and shrinkage refunded after; if the host lacks room the charge is undone and the call is `CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE` with `details.resource`. Other errors: `UNSUPPORTED` for a provider instance or a flavor with a different GPU count, `INVALID_STATE` when the instance is not stopped (both `state` and `desiredState`) or holds no allocation, `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or archived flavor, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` when the growth does not fit. Publishes `instance.resized`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Sets `desiredState` to `deleted` and wakes the reconciler, which releases the allocation, IP lease and quota; returns the instance at once.
methods.description:
Sets `desiredState` to `deleted` and wakes the reconciler, which releases the allocation, IP lease and quota; returns the instance at once.

The call is idempotent: an instance already `deleted` is returned unchanged, and stays readable through `get`. Publishes `instance.deleting`; `instance.deleted` follows when everything is released.

overview: A node's hardware and software inventory as the daemon reports it, kept as an append-only history of snapshots: a new snapshot is stored each time the node's reported section set changes. Every method decides `compute:nodes:read` on `compute-node/{nodeId}` and only answers for nodes the calling tenant owns. See [Inventory and health](/docs/guides/nodes/inventory-and-health).

methods.summary: Returns the node's latest inventory snapshot: its hash, its sections and when it was collected.
methods.description:
Returns the node's latest inventory snapshot: its hash, its sections and when it was collected.

`NOT_FOUND` when the node has no inventory yet or is not owned by the tenant.

methods.summary: Lists the node's inventory snapshots newest first; returns a page with a cursor.
methods.description:
Lists the node's inventory snapshots newest first; returns a page with a cursor.

`limit` is at most 100 (20 by default). The cursor is the id of the last snapshot returned. `NOT_FOUND` when the node is not owned by the tenant.

methods.summary: Compares two of the node's snapshots, named by snapshot id or hash, and returns the changes between them with their stable device ids (GPU UUID, disk WWN or MAC).
methods.description:
Compares two of the node's snapshots, named by snapshot id or hash, and returns the changes between them with their stable device ids (GPU UUID, disk WWN or MAC).

- Without `to`, the latest snapshot is used; without `from`, the snapshot before `to`. A node with a single snapshot diffs against nothing: `from` is empty and there are no changes.
- Change types are `gpu.missing`, `gpu.added`, `disk.replaced`, `driver.changed` and `mig.layout.changed`, each with `before` and `after` values where they apply.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the node has no inventory, a named snapshot does not exist for the node, or the node is not owned by the tenant.

overview: Join requests are the approval queue for joins an attestor deferred: a machine with placeholder hardware identifiers, a machine the `discovery` attestor did not know, or a TPM whose endorsement key is on no allow-list. An approval admits exactly one join, which the machine's retry with the same CSR consumes. The group is decided on `compute-pool/{poolId}` with the join-token actions. See [Joining nodes](/docs/guides/nodes/joining).

methods.summary: Lists the join requests a pool can decide: its own, and its site's requests that no pool has claimed yet.
methods.description:
Lists the join requests a pool can decide: its own, and its site's requests that no pool has claimed yet.

Decided as `compute:join-tokens:read`. `state` defaults to `pending`; `all` lists every state. A pending or approved request past its expiry reads as `expired`, whether or not retention has marked it yet. Pages hold up to 200 requests (100 by default). A pool the tenant does not own is `NOT_FOUND`.

methods.summary: Approves a pending join request, assigns it to the pool and returns it with a new expiry of `ttlSeconds` (60 to 86,400, one hour by default).
methods.description:
Approves a pending join request, assigns it to the pool and returns it with a new expiry of `ttlSeconds` (60 to 86,400, one hour by default).

Decided as `compute:join-tokens:create`. Approving a request that is already approved for this pool returns the approval unchanged. Any other decided state (`rejected`, `expired`, `consumed`) is `INVALID_STATE`, and so is an archived pool. A pool the tenant does not own, or a request the pool cannot see, is `NOT_FOUND`.

Publishes `security.join-request.approved` with the new `expiresAt`.

methods.summary: Rejects a pending join request, or withdraws an approval the machine has not used yet, and returns the request.
methods.description:
Rejects a pending join request, or withdraws an approval the machine has not used yet, and returns the request.

Decided as `compute:join-tokens:create`. Rejecting a request that is already rejected returns it unchanged. An `expired` or `consumed` request is `INVALID_STATE`. A later retry with the request's CSR fails.

Publishes `security.join-request.rejected`, with `reason` when one is given.

overview: Join tokens are single-purpose credentials that let a limited number of daemons join one pool for a limited time. The bearer form `bcjt_<id>.<secret>` is returned once, when the token is created; the control plane stores only the SHA-256 of the secret. Every method is decided on `compute-pool/{poolId}`. See [Joining nodes](/docs/guides/nodes/joining).

methods.summary: Mints a role-`node` join token for one pool and returns its record with the bearer `token`, which is never shown again.
methods.description:
Mints a role-`node` join token for one pool and returns its record with the bearer `token`, which is never shown again.

Only the pool's owner tenant can mint tokens for it; another tenant gets `NOT_FOUND`. A pool whose machines run no daemon (its `agent` is not `bcd`) answers `INVALID_STATE`. `expect` pins the token to one machine and must name at least one identifier, otherwise the call is `INVALID_INPUT`. `ttlSeconds` runs from 60 to 86,400 and `maxUses` defaults to 1.

`hosted: 'kubernetes'` marks a token for `bcd` running as a DaemonSet on a Kubernetes cluster. That cluster's admins have root on its machines, so a node joining with it becomes `tenant-controlled`, with a `node-tenant` certificate that never receives platform secrets. The exception is a pool whose `policy.kubernetes.platformOperated` is true, and only when the platform owns that pool (it is the pool's site's owner, on a site that is not `custom`): anyone who can edit a pool's policy could otherwise vouch for their own cluster, so set it only on pools whose clusters the platform runs. The token decides this, never the machine's claims, and it only ever lowers `platform` trust: a tenant's own site stays `tenant-owned`.

The token id derives from the tenant, the calling identity and `idempotencyKey`. A retry with the same key returns the stored record without `token` and without a new IAM decision. The same key with a different pool, `expect`, `allowReclaim` or `hosted` is `CONFLICT`.

Publishes `security.join-token.created`, whose `pinned` field says whether the token has an `expect` binding; `hosted` is included when set.

methods.summary: Lists a pool's join tokens in id order, never with their secrets.
methods.description:
Lists a pool's join tokens in id order, never with their secrets.

By default only live tokens appear: not revoked, with uses left and not expired. `includeInactive: true` adds used-up, expired and revoked tokens. Pages hold up to 200 tokens (100 by default); pass the returned `cursor` to read the next page.

methods.summary: Revokes a join token at once and returns its record with `revokedAt` set.
methods.description:
Revokes a join token at once and returns its record with `revokedAt` set.

Revoking a token that is already revoked returns it unchanged and publishes nothing. A token that does not exist in the tenant and pool is `NOT_FOUND`. A first revocation publishes `security.join-token.revoked`.

overview: The metal group enrolls machines by their BMCs and moves them through the provision state machine: inspect, commission, deploy, rescue, release and retire. Each verb checks the move against the provision state table, records it in one transaction and queues the metal reconciler, which runs the workflow of the new state; no verb touches the machine itself. Every method returns the node's metal view, which reports whether BMC credentials are set but never returns them. See [Bare metal](/docs/guides/bare-metal) and [BMC drivers and credentials](/docs/guides/bare-metal/bmc).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

siteId.description: The site the node is in (the pool must be in it)

driver.description: The BMC driver id, such as redfish

credentials.description: A secret:// (or vault://, env://) reference, or inline { username, password } stored in the secret broker at once and never echoed

tlsSpkiSha256.description: SHA-256 of the BMC certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, 64 hex digits, to pin its TLS

driverOptions.description: Options for the BMC driver, sent with every BMC operation (e.g. bcx-ipmi { "cipherSuite": 3 } for old BMCs): a JSON object of at most 1 KiB, never credentials. The driver validates its keys

bmc.description: How to reach the node's BMC

macs.description: The node's PXE MAC addresses (':' or '-' separated). Required for a pool with an agent when the BMC driver cannot report them (IPMI)

addresses.description: The machine's own IP addresses, the only hosts site.httpProxy may reach for it (agentless pools); out-of-band inspection replaces them when it reports some

uefi.description: Boots in UEFI mode (false: legacy BIOS)

methods.summary: Creates a metal node from a BMC address, driver and credentials in the given pool, in provision state `enrolling`, and queues the reconciler to verify BMC access and inspect the machine out of band.
methods.description:
Creates a metal node from a BMC address, driver and credentials in the given pool, in provision state `enrolling`, and queues the reconciler to verify BMC access and inspect the machine out of band.

- Decided as `compute:nodes:provision` on the pool, since the node does not exist yet.
- `bmc.credentials` is a `secret://` reference or an inline username and password. Inline credentials go to the secret broker before anything is written, and only the reference is stored; without a secret broker they are `INVALID_CONFIG`.
- The node's driver bindings come from the BMC (power, management, virtual media), then the hardware profile (`hardwareProfile`, else the pool's `policy.hardwareProfile`). An unknown hardware profile is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- `bmc.driverOptions` is a JSON object of at most 1 KiB for the BMC driver (e.g. `{ "cipherSuite": 3 }` for older IPMI BMCs), sent on every BMC request and validated by the driver. Keys that look like credentials are `INVALID_INPUT`: credentials travel only as `bmc.credentials`.
- `addresses` are the machine's own IP literals (at most 16). In an agentless pool the site's agents can reach the machine through them at once; out-of-band inspection replaces them only when it reports some (IPMI reports none). A driver that cannot report MACs needs `macs` given here.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the pool does not exist or the tenant does not own it; `INVALID_INPUT` when the pool is not in `siteId`.

Each call creates a new node; there is no idempotency key. Publishes `node.enrolled`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `ready` node back to `enrolling` to re-verify BMC access; the reconciler then chains re-inspection and re-commissioning back to `ready`.
methods.description:
Moves a `ready` node back to `enrolling` to re-verify BMC access; the reconciler then chains re-inspection and re-commissioning back to `ready`.

`INVALID_STATE` from any state but `ready`, `NOT_FOUND` when the tenant has no such metal node, and `CONFLICT` when the node changed concurrently. Publishes `node.provision.enrolling`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `ready` node to `inspecting`, where the machine boots the ramdisk and reports its inventory; commissioning follows, and the node returns to `ready`.
methods.description:
Moves a `ready` node to `inspecting`, where the machine boots the ramdisk and reports its inventory; commissioning follows, and the node returns to `ready`.

`INVALID_STATE` from any state but `ready`; `CONFLICT` when the node changed concurrently. Publishes `node.provision.inspecting`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `ready` node to `commissioning`, which runs DCGM diagnostics, a quick wipe and a power-off before the node returns to `ready`.
methods.description:
Moves a `ready` node to `commissioning`, which runs DCGM diagnostics, a quick wipe and a power-off before the node returns to `ready`.

`INVALID_STATE` from any state but `ready`; `CONFLICT` when the node changed concurrently. Publishes `node.provision.commissioning`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `ready` node to `deploying` with the given profile version recorded on it; the metal reconciler then starts a workflow of that profile.
methods.description:
Moves a `ready` node to `deploying` with the given profile version recorded on it; the metal reconciler then starts a workflow of that profile.

The call records `profileId` and `profileVersion` without running the profile; run `profiles.validate` first to catch problems before the workflow starts. When the workflow succeeds the node becomes `deployed` and takes the profile's `role`. `INVALID_STATE` from any state but `ready`; `CONFLICT` when the node changed concurrently. Publishes `node.provision.deploying`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

wipe.description: How the disks are wiped on release

methods.summary: Moves a `deployed` or `rescue` node to `releasing`, which wipes its disks with the chosen mode and powers it off before it returns to `ready`.
methods.description:
Moves a `deployed` or `rescue` node to `releasing`, which wipes its disks with the chosen mode and powers it off before it returns to `ready`.

`wipe` is `none`, `quick` (the default), `secure-erase` or `crypto-erase`. Unless the mode is `none`, the node reaches `ready` only when the wipe result is attested; otherwise it fails with `UNVERIFIED_WIPE`. `INVALID_STATE` from other states. Publishes `node.provision.releasing`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `deployed` node to `rescue`, whose workflow boots the rescue ramdisk for repairs from outside the installed OS.
methods.description:
Moves a `deployed` node to `rescue`, whose workflow boots the rescue ramdisk for repairs from outside the installed OS.

`INVALID_STATE` from any state but `deployed`. On a pool with `agent: 'none'` the node fails with `UNSUPPORTED`, since such a machine cannot boot the ramdisk. Publishes `node.provision.rescue`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Starts the `metal-unrescue` workflow, which boots a rescued node back into its installed OS; the node stays in `rescue` until that workflow succeeds, then becomes `deployed`.
methods.description:
Starts the `metal-unrescue` workflow, which boots a rescued node back into its installed OS; the node stays in `rescue` until that workflow succeeds, then becomes `deployed`.

- `INVALID_STATE` outside `rescue`.
- A second call while the unrescue workflow runs returns the node unchanged.
- `CONFLICT` while the rescue ramdisk is still booting.
- `INVALID_CONFIG` when the provision module is not registered.

Publishes `node.provision.unrescuing` with the `workflowId`. If the workflow fails, the node goes to `failed`, and `recover` returns it to `deployed`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

reason.description: Recorded as the node's last error

methods.summary: Stops the node's running workflow and moves the node to `failed`, recording where it failed, an `ABORTED` error with the optional `reason`, and maintenance on.
methods.description:
Stops the node's running workflow and moves the node to `failed`, recording where it failed, an `ABORTED` error with the optional `reason`, and maintenance on.

Legal from `enrolling`, `inspecting`, `commissioning`, `deploying` and `releasing`; `INVALID_STATE` otherwise. The aborted workflow still runs its cleanup steps. Publishes `node.provision.failed`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a `failed` node to the last stable point for the state it failed in: `enrolling` after enrolling, inspecting or commissioning, `releasing` after deploying or releasing, `deployed` after rescue, and `retiring` after retiring.
methods.description:
Moves a `failed` node to the last stable point for the state it failed in: `enrolling` after enrolling, inspecting or commissioning, `releasing` after deploying or releasing, `deployed` after rescue, and `retiring` after retiring.

It clears `failedFrom` and `lastError` but leaves maintenance on. `INVALID_STATE` when the node is not `failed`. Publishes `node.provision.enrolling`, `node.provision.releasing`, `node.provision.deployed` or `node.provision.retiring`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Moves a node to `retiring`, whose workflow crypto-erases the disks (on pools whose machines run `bcd`), powers the machine off and revokes its identity before the node becomes `retired`, which is terminal.
methods.description:
Moves a node to `retiring`, whose workflow crypto-erases the disks (on pools whose machines run `bcd`), powers the machine off and revokes its identity before the node becomes `retired`, which is terminal.

Legal from `adopting`, `adopted`, `enrolling`, `ready` and `failed`; `INVALID_STATE` otherwise, so undeploy a deployed machine first. Publishes `node.provision.retiring`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Queues a `bmc.power` command to the site agent of the node's site and returns its `commandId`; the provision state does not change.
methods.description:
Queues a `bmc.power` command to the site agent of the node's site and returns its `commandId`; the provision state does not change.

- Decided as `compute:nodes:power` on the node.
- `action` is `on`, `off`, `graceful-off`, `reset`, `graceful-restart`, `cycle` or `nmi`.
- `INVALID_STATE` when the node has no BMC credentials, while it is `inspecting`, `commissioning`, `deploying` or `releasing` (a workflow controls its power then), or when no site agent serves its site.

The command expires five minutes after it is queued. Its idempotency key derives from the request id, so a retry with the same `X-Request-Id` header returns the same command.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

poolId.description: The pool every node is in

nodeIds.description: The nodes, all in the tenant

wipe.description: undeploy: how the disks are wiped on release

reason.description: What the batch is for: the approvers see it

methods.summary: Runs one lifecycle verb on many nodes of a pool at once (`manage`, `inspect`, `provide`, `undeploy`, `rescue` or `retire`), as one batch; returns every node and, when the verb sends destructive commands, the batch.
methods.description:
Runs one lifecycle verb on many nodes of a pool at once (`manage`, `inspect`, `provide`, `undeploy`, `rescue` or `retire`), as one batch; returns every node and, when the verb sends destructive commands, the batch.

- Each node is decided on its own, exactly as if the verb were called for it (`metal.<verb>`); one refusal refuses the whole call before anything changes. Every node must be in `poolId` (`INVALID_INPUT` otherwise), listed once, 1 to 10,000 of them.
- When the verb's steps send destructive commands, a quorum batch (`commandBatches`) is created over them with `reason`, and each node's commands carry it: with approver keys they wait for its approval; without, it is recorded for audit.
- `wipe` applies to `undeploy` only.

Decided as `compute:nodes:provision` on the pool, then per node.

overview: Nodes are machines that joined the control plane, as their tenant sees them: a tenant sees the nodes the authorization projection holds for it. Every method except `list` is decided on `compute-node/{nodeId}`. Mutations take an optional `version`; when the node has moved past it, the call is `CONFLICT`. See [Operating nodes](/docs/guides/nodes/operating-nodes).

methods.summary: Lists the nodes visible to the tenant in id order, filtered by pool, site, `cordoned` or `provisionState`.
methods.description:
Lists the nodes visible to the tenant in id order, filtered by pool, site, `cordoned` or `provisionState`.

The call is decided once on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`, then each node is checked for `compute:nodes:read`; nodes the caller may not read are left out, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` items. Pages hold up to 50 nodes.

methods.summary: Returns one node with its labels, conditions and session (epoch, gateway and connection times).
methods.description:
Returns one node with its labels, conditions and session (epoch, gateway and connection times).

A node the tenant cannot see is `NOT_FOUND`.

methods.summary: Returns a node's events from the event outbox, oldest first.
methods.description:
Returns a node's events from the event outbox, oldest first.

`type` keeps only events whose type starts with the given prefix, such as `node.` or `security.`. Pages hold up to 200 events (100 by default). A node the tenant cannot see is `NOT_FOUND`.

methods.summary: Marks the node cordoned so placement puts no new work on it; existing allocations stay.
methods.description:
Marks the node cordoned so placement puts no new work on it; existing allocations stay.

Cordoning a cordoned node returns it unchanged and publishes nothing. Otherwise the node's version goes up, its reconciler is queued, and `node.cordoned` is published.

methods.summary: Clears `cordoned` and ends a drain in progress, so the node is placeable again.
methods.description:
Clears `cordoned` and ends a drain in progress, so the node is placeable again.

Decided as `compute:nodes:cordon`. A node that is neither cordoned nor draining is returned unchanged. Otherwise the `draining` reason is removed and `node.uncordoned` is published.

methods.summary: Cordons the node, adds the `draining` NoSchedule reason and hands the node to the Drain controller.
methods.description:
Cordons the node, adds the `draining` NoSchedule reason and hands the node to the Drain controller.

The Drain controller releases nothing in this release: it waits until the node holds no live allocation, then removes `draining` and publishes `node.drained`. The node stays cordoned until `uncordon`. Draining a node that is already draining returns it unchanged. A new drain publishes `node.draining`.

methods.summary: Sets and removes operator labels on the node and returns the node with its labels.
methods.description:
Sets and removes operator labels on the node and returns the node with its labels.

`set` takes up to 64 labels and `remove` up to 64 keys. The call is `INVALID_INPUT` when it names nothing, names a key in both `set` and `remove`, or sets a key that inventory or the system owns. `remove` removes only operator labels. The node's version goes up and `node.labeled` is published.

methods.summary: Adds and removes operator NoSchedule taints, stored in `noScheduleReasons` as `taint:<key>`.
methods.description:
Adds and removes operator NoSchedule taints, stored in `noScheduleReasons` as `taint:<key>`.

`add` and `remove` take up to 32 keys each. The call is `INVALID_INPUT` when it names nothing or names a key in both lists. Only operator taints change; conditions, `unreachable` and `draining` belong to their controllers. When the result equals the current reasons the node is returned unchanged; otherwise `node.tainted` is published.

methods.summary: Re-runs acceptance checks on a node in `adopting` or `adopted`, moving it to `adopting`.
methods.description:
Re-runs acceptance checks on a node in `adopting` or `adopted`, moving it to `adopting`.

Decided as `compute:nodes:provision`. Any other provision state is `INVALID_STATE`. The node leaves placement until acceptance passes. Publishes `node.adopting`.

methods.summary: Revokes every live certificate of the node and raises its identity generation, so no certificate of the old generation can renew.
methods.description:
Revokes every live certificate of the node and raises its identity generation, so no certificate of the old generation can renew.

Returns the node and `revokedCertificates`, the number of certificates revoked; the revocation reason is `reason`, or `identity revoked`. Each call raises the generation again. The machine comes back only by joining again. Publishes `security.node.identity-revoked`.

methods.summary: Tombstones a node that is `retired`, `adopting` or `enrolling` (or failed from `adopting` or `enrolling`) and has no open allocation.
methods.description:
Tombstones a node that is `retired`, `adopting` or `enrolling` (or failed from `adopting` or `enrolling`) and has no open allocation.

Any other state, or an open allocation, is `INVALID_STATE`; a node that changed pools during the call is `CONFLICT`. The node's devices stop being bookable, its scalar resources are removed, its certificates are revoked, its hardware key and attestor bindings are freed so the machine can join again as a new node, and its pending commands are cancelled. The node leaves its pool and the projection, so nobody sees it; audit rows and past allocations keep referencing it.

A retry after the delete returns `deleted: false`. Publishes `node.deleted`.

publicKey.description: Your OpenSSH public key line (Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256)

principal.description: The Unix account to log in as, one of the deployment's sshAccounts

methods.summary: Issues a short-lived break-glass OpenSSH user certificate for one node, bound to the principal `<account>@<nodeId>`.
methods.description:
Issues a short-lived break-glass OpenSSH user certificate for one node, bound to the principal `<account>@<nodeId>`.

Decided as `compute:nodes:ssh-root`. The method comes from the tunnels module (v0.3) and is `UNSUPPORTED` when no compute SSH CA is configured. It needs an MFA session by default (`ACCESS_DENIED` with reason `mfa-required`), and a session that ends within a minute is `ACCESS_DENIED`. `publicKey` must be an Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256 key, and `principal` (default `root`) one of the configured accounts; otherwise `INVALID_INPUT`.

The lifetime is `ttlSeconds` (60 to 3,600, default 900), never past the caller's session. Issuance is rate-limited per identity (20 per hour by default, then `RATE_LIMITED`). Every certificate is recorded and `node.ssh-cert.issued` is published.

serial.description: The certificate serial in decimal, as nodes.issueSshCert returned it

methods.summary: Revokes a break-glass SSH certificate before it expires; the node's revocation list carries it from the next NodeSpec on.
methods.description:
Revokes a break-glass SSH certificate before it expires; the node's revocation list carries it from the next NodeSpec on.

Decided as `compute:nodes:ssh-root` and hosted by the tunnels module (v0.3). Revoking again returns the same revocation. A serial not issued for this node is `NOT_FOUND`. Publishes `node.ssh-cert.revoked`.

includeExpired.description: Also certificates past their expiry (kept one day)

methods.summary: Lists the break-glass SSH certificates the tenant issued for one node, newest first, with each one's principal, issuer, lifetime and state; never the certificate itself.
methods.description:
Lists the break-glass SSH certificates the tenant issued for one node, newest first, with each one's principal, issuer, lifetime and state; never the certificate itself.

Decided as `compute:nodes:read` on `compute-node/{nodeId}` and hosted by the tunnels module. `state` is `active`, `expired` or `revoked`; a revoked certificate also carries `revokedAt`, `revokedBy` (an identity, or `iam` when re-authorization revoked it) and `revokeReason` when one was given.

Only unexpired certificates are listed unless `includeExpired` is true; expired certificates are kept for one day, then removed by an hourly clean-up. Pages hold 1 to 500 certificates (100 by default), and `nextCursor` is set while more remain. A node the tenant cannot see is `NOT_FOUND`, and a malformed `cursor` is `INVALID_INPUT`.

overview: A pool groups the nodes of one site under one GPU model, one sharing mode and one policy, and every reservation and quota belongs to exactly one pool. The tenant that creates a pool owns it; other tenants see it only once the owner offers it to them with a quota. Only the owner can offer, unoffer, update or archive a pool; anyone else gets `NOT_FOUND`. See [Pools](/docs/guides/capacity/pools).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns the pools the tenant owns or is offered, each with `owned`, `archived` and the tenant's own quota rows.
methods.description:
Returns the pools the tenant owns or is offered, each with `owned`, `archived` and the tenant's own quota rows.

Archived pools appear only for their owner. After the coarse decision on the tenant, each pool is checked as `compute:pools:read` on the pool, and only the allowed ones are returned.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

methods.summary: Returns one pool as the tenant sees it, with `owned`, `archived` and the tenant's own quota rows.
methods.description:
Returns one pool as the tenant sees it, with `owned`, `archived` and the tenant's own quota rows.

The call is `NOT_FOUND` when the pool is not owned by or offered to the tenant, or is archived and the tenant is not its owner.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

siteId.description: The site the pool lives in

agent.description: bcd (default), or none for provider pools

ownerQuota.description: The owner's limits per resource (default: unlimited GPUs)

providerAccountId.description: Provider pools: the provider account behind them

idempotencyKey.description: Makes the pool id deterministic; a retry returns the pool

methods.summary: Creates a pool on a site the tenant owns, with the owner's quota rows and an empty rollup; returns the pool at version 1.
methods.description:
Creates a pool on a site the tenant owns, with the owner's quota rows and an empty rollup; returns the pool at version 1.

- It is decided as `compute:pools:create` on the tenant (`compute-tenant`), the alternative its catalog row lists next to `compute-fleet`.

overview: A reservation is a tenant's claim on devices of one pool for a time window. `create` first writes the request as a draft, Better IAM decides once on that draft with the request as attributes, and only an allowed draft is charged against quota and placed. A reservation holds its quota charge until it reaches a terminal state, and the `capacity.reservations` reconciler drives it through `placed`, `binding` and `active` to `released`. See [Reservations](/docs/guides/capacity/reservations).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

selector.description: matchExpressions over device attributes, then node labels

binding.description: hold (CDI devices), node (a whole-node lease in a tenantRoot pool) or kubernetes (the devices advertised to the node’s kubelet, in a pool with policy.kubernetes)

idempotencyKey.description: Scoped to (tenant, caller identity): a retry with the same key replays

methods.summary: Books devices of one pool for a time window after one IAM decision on the draft; returns the reservation, `placed` or `pending`.
methods.description:
Books devices of one pool for a time window after one IAM decision on the draft; returns the reservation, `placed` or `pending`.

- **Idempotency.** The reservation id is derived from the tenant, the caller's identity and `idempotencyKey`. The same key with the same request returns the stored reservation without a second decision once it is past the draft stage, and decides the same draft again while it is still a draft. The same key with a different request is `CONFLICT`, with `details.reservationId`; a key whose request was refused stays `ACCESS_DENIED`. `wait` is not part of the compared request.
- **Decision.** `compute:reservations:create` is decided on the draft (`compute-reservation`), with attributes such as `gpuModel`, `gpuCount`, `durationHours` and `region`. When an agent in a delegated session is refused and IAM opens a confirmation request, the call fails with `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and the draft waits in `awaiting-confirmation` for at most 30 minutes; a retry with the same key after approval continues it.
- **Errors.** `NOT_FOUND` when the pool is not owned by or offered to the tenant, or is archived. `INVALID_INPUT` when a device class or sharing mode does not match the pool's, `binding: 'node'` names a pool without `policy.tenantRoot`, `binding: 'kubernetes'` names a pool without `policy.kubernetes`, or a node binding asks for `resources`. `UNSUPPORTED` for any binding other than `hold`, `node` or `kubernetes`. `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` when the charge does not fit; the draft stays, so the same key can be retried. `SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED` when the pool or the tenant's offer asks for a budget check and the budget is spent.
- **Host resources.** `resources` (`vcpu`, `memoryGiB`, `hugepages1Gi`, per node for a gang) books host CPU, memory and 1 GiB hugepages on the same node as the devices, and the node enforces them. Without it, a request for whole GPUs books the pool's per-GPU share, stored on the reservation at creation. That share is `policy.perGpu` where it is set, or otherwise the smallest share any of the pool's GPU hosts can give (its allocatable CPUs or memory divided by its bookable GPUs). Requests for MIG instances or slots alone, and pools whose hosts report no CPU or memory rows, book none. Host resources are not charged to quota: the GPUs are.
- **Placement.** A request that does not fit, and is not spot, may preempt spot work. Otherwise it is `pending` with an `Unschedulable` condition and retried every 30 seconds, or, with the pool-lease placer, `pending` with a `Queued` condition. `wait.timeoutMs` (at most 30 seconds) holds the answer while the reservation is queued; a timeout returns the reservation still queued, not an error.

Emits `reservation.placed`, `reservation.pending`, `reservation.queued` or `reservation.awaiting-confirmation`.

Returns one reservation of the tenant with its `operation` and, once a node reported its devices bound, its `binding`.

Returns the tenant's reservations newest first, skipping drafts, filtered by `state` and `poolId`, one page at a time.

With `scope: 'mine'` (the default) only the caller's own reservations are listed. With `scope: 'all'` the tenant's reservations are loaded and each one is checked as `compute:reservations:read` on the reservation, so only the allowed ones are returned. `limit` is 1 to 200, default 50; `cursor` is the id of the last reservation of the previous page, and the answer carries the next `cursor` while more remain.

Ends a reservation now: its bookings are released at `compute_now()`, its quota is refunded, and it becomes `released`; returns the reservation.

A `pending` reservation is `cancelled` instead. A reservation already in a terminal state is returned unchanged. A request still in `draft` or `awaiting-confirmation` is `INVALID_STATE`. Freed capacity wakes the pool's pending reservations. Emits `reservation.released` or `reservation.cancelled`, with `reason: 'release'`.

methods.description:
Withdraws a reservation that has not started (`pending` or `placed`): its bookings are released, its quota is refunded, and it becomes `cancelled`; returns the reservation.

A reservation already `cancelled` is returned unchanged. Any other state is `INVALID_STATE`; use `release` for a reservation that has started. Drafts are `NOT_FOUND`. It is decided as `compute:reservations:release`. Emits `reservation.cancelled`.

methods.summary: Moves the end of a `placed`, `binding` or `active` reservation later, all or nothing, after one IAM decision; returns the reservation and whether it was extended.
methods.description:
Moves the end of a `placed`, `binding` or `active` reservation later, all or nothing, after one IAM decision; returns the reservation and whether it was extended.

- Give exactly one of `until` (a new end, epoch milliseconds) or `by` (a duration); both or neither is `INVALID_INPUT`. Other states are `INVALID_STATE`.
- It is admitted like `create`: the pending change goes into the reservation's authz row with `durationHours` set to the total after the change, so a policy that caps duration also caps extensions. A refusal is `ACCESS_DENIED` and clears the pending change. `SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED` applies as for `create`.
- When another booking starts before the new end, nothing moves and the answer is `extended: false` with `availableUntil`, the latest end the bookings can reach.
- **Idempotency.** An `until` the reservation already reaches answers `extended: false` without a decision, so a retried `until` is safe. `idempotencyKey` does not replay: a repeated `by` extends again from the new end.
- While another extend of the same reservation is being decided, the call is `CONFLICT` with `details.reason: 'extend-in-flight'` and `retryAfterSeconds`.

Emits `reservation.extended` with the new `end`.

Moves the lease deadline of a renewable reservation to now plus its `leaseSeconds`, without changing its window; returns the reservation.

A reservation created without `leaseSeconds` is `INVALID_STATE`, as is one not in `placed`, `binding` or `active`. A lease that lapses without renewal releases the reservation with reason `lease-lapsed`. It is decided as `compute:reservations:extend`. Renewing emits no event.

overview: Rollouts take a registered bcd release to the nodes of the tenant's pools in waves, within each pool's disruption budget. A controller settles nodes as they report the new version, pauses the rollout when a wave's failure ratio exceeds its limit, and soaks between waves. Every method decides `compute:fleet:admin` on the fleet scope. See [Rollouts](/docs/guides/rollouts).

methods.description:
Plans a rollout of a registered release to every node that runs bcd in the tenant's pools, or in `poolIds`, and starts it; returns the rollout in `running`.

- **Plan.** Nodes are shuffled by a hash of the rollout id and assigned to `waves`, cumulative percentages that must increase and end at 100 (default 1, 10, 50, 100). The other gates default to `maxFailureRatio` 0.05, `soakSeconds` 600 and `upgradeTimeoutSeconds` 900. Nodes that already report the version start as `succeeded`.
- **Idempotency.** `idempotencyKey` is optional. With a key, the rollout id derives from the tenant, the caller and the key: a repeat for the same version returns the existing rollout, and another version under the key is `CONFLICT`.
- **Errors.** `NOT_FOUND` when the version is not registered or a listed pool is not an unarchived pool of the tenant. `INVALID_STATE` when no node in scope runs bcd yet. `CONFLICT` with `details.rolloutId` when a node in scope is in another running or paused rollout. `INVALID_INPUT` for gates out of range.
- **Events.** `rollout.started`; the controller later publishes `rollout.wave`, `rollout.paused` and `rollout.completed`.

Warm instances are owned by the template's author, placed and charged to quota when they are created, and a refill that fails is logged and tried again on a later pass. See [Sandboxes](/docs/guides/vps/sandboxes).

methods.description:
Checks the pool, flavor, image and runtime once and stores a template under a name unique in the tenant; returns the template.

- **Checks.** The pool must be owned by or offered to the tenant and not archived (`NOT_FOUND`), and be a hosted `vps-host` pool: a provider pool is `INVALID_INPUT`. A missing or archived flavor and an image that does not resolve are `NOT_FOUND`; `INVALID_CONFIG` when `vps()` has no `images`. The pool's runtime must boot the image's format and pass through the flavor's GPUs (`INVALID_INPUT`), and `runtime`, when given, must equal the pool's runtime (`INVALID_INPUT`). The template stores the pool's runtime.
- **Lifetime.** `defaultTtlSeconds` defaults to 3,600 and `maxTtlSeconds` to 86,400 or the default TTL, whichever is larger; both lie between 60 seconds and 30 days, and a default above the maximum is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- **Warm pool.** `warm.min` and `warm.max` are 0 to 64; `max` defaults to `min`, and a `max` below `min` is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- **User data.** At most 32 KiB. A URI must be a `secret://` reference to a secret of the same tenant, otherwise `INVALID_INPUT`.
- **Volumes.** `volumes` lists up to 8 sandbox volumes (`sandboxVolumes`) that each sandbox of the template attaches:
  - each entry names a volume by `volumeId` or by `name` (one of them), with a `mountPath` and an optional `readOnly`;
  - each volume must be the tenant's, `ready` and in the template's pool (`NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_STATE`, `INVALID_INPUT`), and named once;
  - a mount path is absolute, without `.` or `..`, never over a system directory (`/`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/proc`, …), and never inside another entry's (`INVALID_INPUT`);
  - a template with volumes keeps no warm pool (`warm.max` must be 0), since a warm instance would hold the volumes.

  Its sandboxes run on the volumes' host only. A read-write attachment needs the volume to itself, so a second sandbox of a template that attaches a volume read-write is `CONFLICT` (`details.reason: 'volume-in-use'`) while the first lives.

A live template with the same name is `CONFLICT`. The caller becomes the template's owner in the authorization projection. Publishes no event.

overview: Sandbox volumes are persistent disks on one host that a tenant's sandboxes attach across runs, so an agent keeps its memory, caches and checkouts. A volume is placed when it is created: its size is booked as `diskGiB` on one host of the pool, charged to the tenant's quota, and the host keeps it as a sparse qcow2 file. A sandbox template names volumes with a mount path. Sandboxes of that template then run on the volume's host only, attach it as an extra virtio disk, and mount it by serial (`/dev/disk/by-id/virtio-<serial>`) from their user data. The first mount formats it as ext4, and no later one ever does. A volume takes any number of read-only attachments or one read-write attachment, never both. Volumes are metered as `vps.volume.gib.hours` from creation until the disk is released. See [Sandboxes](/docs/guides/vps/sandboxes).

overview: A sandbox is a hosted VPS instance with a template and a lifetime: `create` admits it after one IAM decision, then claims a warm instance of its template or creates one through the instance lifecycle, and the `vps.sandboxes` reconciler, which runs every 15 seconds, deletes it once `expiresAt` passes. A sandbox's `state` follows its instance: `starting`, `ready` while the instance runs, `failed` when it is in `error` or `lost`, `deleting` once deletion was asked, and `deleted` when the instance is gone. The instance belongs to the sandbox: `instances.start`, `stop`, `resize` and `delete` refuse it with `INVALID_STATE`, and `instances.get` still returns it. See [Sandboxes](/docs/guides/vps/sandboxes).

methods.summary: Starts a sandbox from a template after one IAM decision on the draft, claiming a warm instance when the template holds one and creating a new instance otherwise; the lifetime starts at once.
methods.description:
Starts a sandbox from a template after one IAM decision on the draft, claiming a warm instance when the template holds one and creating a new instance otherwise; the lifetime starts at once.

- **Idempotency.** `idempotencyKey` is required. The sandbox id derives from the tenant, the caller's identity and the key: a retry of an admitted request returns the stored sandbox without a second decision, and a different request under the same key is `CONFLICT` with `details.sandboxId`, as is the key replayed by another agent or person. `wait` is not part of the compared request.
- **IAM.** `compute:sandboxes:create` is decided on `compute-sandbox/` plus the draft id, whose parent is the template's pool. Policies can test `templateId`, `vcpu`, `memoryGiB`, `gpus`, `ttlSeconds` and `warm` (true when the template keeps a warm pool). A refusal deletes the draft; a delegated session can get `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`. After an allow, the pool's budget check can answer `SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED` and keep the draft for a retry with the same key.
- **Start.** The oldest stopped or paused warm instance of the template is claimed: it changes owner to the caller, is set to run, and publishes `instance.starting`; the claim places nothing new. Without one, a new instance is created and placed as `instances.create` would, publishing `instance.created` and, once placed, `instance.scheduled`; when no host fits it waits in scheduling and the sandbox stays `starting`. `warm` in the answer tells which path was taken.
- **Restore.** `fromSnapshot` starts the sandbox from one of the tenant's own `ready` snapshots of this template, taken on its runtime (another tenant's is `NOT_FOUND`, one not ready is `INVALID_STATE`, one of another template is `INVALID_INPUT`). An agent restores only snapshots of sandboxes it created itself; any other is `NOT_FOUND` to it. A restore never claims a warm instance, and a snapshot that includes memory places only on nodes with the same `cpu.model`. Policies see it as the `fromSnapshot` attribute.
- **Lifetime.** `ttlSeconds` defaults to the template's `defaultTtlSeconds` and may not exceed its `maxTtlSeconds` (`INVALID_INPUT`). `expiresAt` is set when the sandbox is admitted.
- **Errors.** `NOT_FOUND` for a template missing or deleted in the tenant. `INVALID_STATE` when the template's flavor has been archived or removed. On the new-instance path the template's pool, flavor and image are checked again, with the errors of `sandboxTemplates.create`; `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` when the shape does not fit the tenant's quota and `CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE` when the pool has no free IP address, both keeping the draft.
- **Waiting.** `wait.timeoutMs` (at most 30 seconds) holds the answer until the sandbox leaves `starting`; a timeout returns it still `starting`, not an error.

Publishes `sandbox.created` with `warm` and `expiresAt`. `sandbox.ready` follows from the reconciler once the instance first runs.

methods.description:
Returns a page of the tenant's sandboxes, newest first, with a `cursor` when more remain.

`scope` defaults to `mine`, the caller's own sandboxes, which needs no per-item check. `all` lists every sandbox of the tenant, each one checked for `compute:sandboxes:read`; those the caller may not read are left out, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` items. Deleted sandboxes are left out unless `deleted` is true, and `templateId` keeps one template's sandboxes. `limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50); `cursor` is the last sandbox id of the previous page. Drafts are never listed. Each item carries `identityRebound` as `get` describes.

methods.description:
Returns one sandbox of the tenant with its state, its instance's state, addresses and node, and its `expiresAt`.

`readyAt` is set once the reconciler saw the instance run, and `expiredAt` when the sandbox ended by reaching `expiresAt`. `snapshots` lists the sandbox's snapshots with their state. Drafts and sandboxes of other tenants are `NOT_FOUND`.

`identityRebound` appears only on a memory restore that was given its own guest identity. It is `false` until the host has installed that identity; until then the guest still answers to its source's identity, and `exec` is refused with `restore-shares-identity` while another guest shares it. It is `true` once the identity is installed, from which point `exec` signs for this sandbox alone. It is absent when there is nothing to install: the sandbox is not a memory restore, or exec is not configured.
