methods.summary: Moves a sandbox's `expiresAt` later after one IAM decision, within its template's `maxTtlSeconds` counted from creation; returns the sandbox.
methods.description:
Moves a sandbox's `expiresAt` later after one IAM decision, within its template's `maxTtlSeconds` counted from creation; returns the sandbox.

- Give exactly one of `until` (the new expiry, epoch milliseconds) or `by` (added to the current expiry: `30m`, `8h`, `7d`, or milliseconds, at most 30 days); both or neither is `INVALID_INPUT`. A lifetime past the template's `maxTtlSeconds` is `INVALID_INPUT`, and a sandbox whose deletion has started, by `delete` or by expiry, is `INVALID_STATE`.
- **IAM.** `compute:sandboxes:update` is decided on the sandbox with a pending `ttlSeconds` equal to the whole lifetime after the change, so a policy that caps `ttlSeconds` on `create` also caps extensions. A refusal is `ACCESS_DENIED` and clears the pending change.
- **Idempotency.** An `until` that is not later than the current expiry returns the sandbox unchanged without a decision, so a retried `until` is safe. There is no `idempotencyKey`: a repeated `by` extends again.
- While another extend of the same sandbox is being decided, the call is `CONFLICT` with `details.reason: 'extend-in-flight'` and `retryAfterSeconds`. A spent budget is `SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED`.

The stored `ttlSeconds` becomes the new whole lifetime. Publishes `sandbox.extended` with the new `expiresAt`.

methods.description:
Saves a running or paused sandbox's state (disk, and memory unless `includeMemory` is false) as a tenant-private snapshot; returns it `pending` until the host's `instance.snapshot` command settles.

- **Where.** The deployment's snapshot store (`vps({ snapshots })`) presigns an https upload URL, and the host uploads straight to it. Without a store the call is `INVALID_CONFIG`. A sandbox that is not running or paused, or whose deletion has started, is `INVALID_STATE`.
- **Settling.** The `vps.sandboxes` reconciler, woken when the command settles, makes the snapshot `ready` (with its sha256, size, runtime and CPU model) and publishes `sandbox.snapshot.ready`, or makes it `failed` and publishes `sandbox.snapshot.failed`.
- **Idempotency.** With `idempotencyKey`, a retry returns the same snapshot; the key used for another sandbox is `CONFLICT`. Without one, every call takes a new snapshot.
- **Lifetime.** A snapshot is deleted with its sandbox unless `keep` is true. A tenant teardown deletes all of them, kept ones included. Snapshots are never promoted to shared images.

methods.summary: Opens SSH into a running sandbox: returns a single-use `ssh` tunnel ticket for its instance and a short OpenSSH user certificate from the deployment's sandbox SSH CA for the principal `<account>@<instanceId>`.
methods.description:
Opens SSH into a running sandbox: returns a single-use `ssh` tunnel ticket for its instance and a short OpenSSH user certificate from the deployment's sandbox SSH CA for the principal `<account>@<instanceId>`.

- **How.** A sandbox has no in-guest agent: the node's daemon dials the instance's own address, and the instance's sshd trusts the sandbox CA and accepts only its own principal, so a certificate for one sandbox opens no other. Open `GET` on the returned `path` with the ticket before `expiresAt`, then speak SSH over it. `better-compute sandbox exec` does both.
- **Host key.** The answer tells whether the guest can be pinned. `hostCertificate` is `valid` when the guest presents a host certificate from the sandbox CA, still good for at least a minute (then pin it with `@cert-authority` for `hostPrincipal` and `HostKeyAlias`). It is `expired` when that certificate ended, and `none` when the instance was never certified. `hostCertified` is true only when `valid`.
- **Certificate.** `publicKey` must be an Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256 key. `ttlSeconds` is 60 to 900 (default 600) and never past the caller's session. Guests receive no revocation list, so the short lifetime is the revocation control, and tunnel re-authorization closes the transport.
- **Errors.** `UNSUPPORTED` when the deployment has no sandbox SSH CA (`tunnels.sandboxSsh`). `ACCESS_DENIED` for an API key (reason `session-required`) or a session ending within a minute. `INVALID_STATE` when the sandbox is not running or is being deleted, and with `details.reason: 'restore-shares-identity'` while another running guest shares its SSH identity (a memory restore of the same snapshot, or the sandbox it was taken from): a certificate for one would open the others, so exec waits until only one of them runs. The node must be connected and advertise `tunnel.instance-dial`. Exec shares the per-identity tunnel rate limit with `tunnels.open` (`RATE_LIMITED`).

Hosted by the tunnels module. Publishes `tunnel.issued`.

methods.summary: Asks for the sandbox's instance to be deleted and marks the sandbox `deleting`; returns the sandbox at once.
methods.description:
Asks for the sandbox's instance to be deleted and marks the sandbox `deleting`; returns the sandbox at once.

The instance's `desiredState` becomes `deleted` and the `vps.instances` reconciler releases its allocation, IP lease and quota as for any instance, publishing `instance.deleting` with the `sandboxId`. The call is idempotent: a sandbox already deleting is returned in its current state. Drafts and missing sandboxes are `NOT_FOUND`.

When the instance is gone, the `vps.sandboxes` reconciler marks the sandbox deleted, removes it from the authorization projection and publishes `sandbox.deleted` with `expired: false`. Expiry takes the same path after publishing `sandbox.expired`, and its `sandbox.deleted` carries `expired: true`.

overview: Secrets are write-only: `put` hands a value to the configured secret store and returns its `secret://` reference and version, and no method ever reads a value back. Events and audit rows carry only the reference, name and version; values reach agents through the secret broker, never through the API. Methods are decided on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`, or on `compute-fleet/global` for platform secrets with `scope: 'fleet'` in the root tenant. See [Security](/docs/operations/security) and [BMC credentials](/docs/guides/bare-metal/bmc).

methods.summary: Stores a secret value under a name and returns its reference and version; a second put with the same name writes a new version.
methods.description:
Stores a secret value under a name and returns its reference and version; a second put with the same name writes a new version.

The value is at most 64 KiB. A retry whose `idempotencyKey` equals the key of the put that wrote the current version returns that version and writes nothing; the key is not scoped to the calling identity. `scope: 'fleet'` outside the root tenant is `INVALID_INPUT`. The call is `UNAVAILABLE` when no secret store is configured, and `INVALID_STATE` when the existing secret lives in another store than the configured one.

Publishes `security.secret.put` with the reference, name and version, never the value.

methods.summary: Deletes a secret's value from the store and its reference, returning `deleted: true`, or `deleted: false` when no such secret exists.
methods.description:
Deletes a secret's value from the store and its reference, returning `deleted: true`, or `deleted: false` when no such secret exists.

`scope: 'fleet'` outside the root tenant is `INVALID_INPUT`. The call is `UNAVAILABLE` when no secret store is configured, and `INVALID_STATE` when the secret lives in another store than the configured one. Publishes `security.secret.deleted`.

overview: Site tokens are join tokens with the role `site`: they enroll `bcd site` agents on one site, which then contend for the site's boot lease. They share the join-token bearer format `bcjt_<id>.<secret>` and storage, so the secret is shown once and only its hash is kept. Both methods are decided as `compute:sites:manage` on `compute-site/{siteId}`. See [Sites](/docs/guides/bare-metal/sites).

methods.summary: Mints a role-`site` join token for one site and returns its record with the bearer `token`, which is never shown again.
methods.description:
Mints a role-`site` join token for one site and returns its record with the bearer `token`, which is never shown again.

Only the site's owner tenant can mint tokens (the root tenant for platform sites); another tenant gets `NOT_FOUND`, and a deleted site is `INVALID_STATE`. `ttlSeconds` runs from 60 to 86,400, and `maxUses` from 1 to 16 (default 1).

The token id derives from the tenant, the calling identity and `idempotencyKey`. A retry with the same key returns the stored record without `token` and without a new IAM decision; the same key for a different site is `CONFLICT`. Publishes `security.site-token.created`.

methods.summary: Revokes a site token at once and returns its record with `revokedAt` set.
methods.description:
Revokes a site token at once and returns its record with `revokedAt` set.

Revoking a token that is already revoked returns it unchanged and publishes nothing. A token that is not a site token of this tenant and site is `NOT_FOUND`. A first revocation publishes `security.site-token.revoked`.

overview: Sites are boot and failure domains: every pool and node belongs to one site. Platform sites (`shared`, `dedicated`) belong to the root tenant; a tenant's own hardware lives on its `custom` sites. A tenant sees the sites the authorization projection holds for it. See [Sites](/docs/guides/bare-metal/sites).

methods.summary: Lists the sites visible to the tenant in id order, filtered by `kind` or `region`.
methods.description:
Lists the sites visible to the tenant in id order, filtered by `kind` or `region`.

The call is decided once on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`, then each site is checked for `compute:sites:read`; sites the caller may not read are left out, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` items. Pages hold up to 50 sites.

methods.summary: Returns one site: its kind, region, IAM region and version.
methods.description:
Returns one site: its kind, region, IAM region and version.

A site the tenant cannot see is `NOT_FOUND`.

methods.summary: Creates a site and adds it to the authorization projection with its region and kind as IAM attributes.
methods.description:
Creates a site and adds it to the authorization projection with its region and kind as IAM attributes.

A `custom` site is decided on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`; a `shared` or `dedicated` site on `compute-fleet/global`, and its `tenantId` must be the root tenant, otherwise the call is `INVALID_INPUT`. `iamRegion` names the IAM region when it differs from `region`.

The site id derives from the tenant, the calling identity and `idempotencyKey`. A retry with the same key returns the site without a new IAM decision; the same key with a different kind, region or IAM region is `CONFLICT`. Publishes `site.created`.

methods.summary: Changes a site's `region` or `iamRegion`, or clears `iamRegion` so IAM uses `region`, and returns the site.
methods.description:
Changes a site's `region` or `iamRegion`, or clears `iamRegion` so IAM uses `region`, and returns the site.

Only the owner tenant can update a site; a deleted site is `NOT_FOUND`. Naming no change, or both `iamRegion` and `clearIamRegion`, is `INVALID_INPUT`, and a stale `version` is `CONFLICT`. An update that changes nothing returns the site unchanged. Otherwise the new attributes reach every tenant that sees the site, and `site.updated` is published.

methods.summary: Deletes a site that has no unarchived pool and no undeleted node.
methods.description:
Deletes a site that has no unarchived pool and no undeleted node.

Only the owner tenant can delete a site. A site with live pools or nodes is `INVALID_STATE`, and a stale `version` is `CONFLICT`. The call revokes the site's join and site tokens, expires its pending and approved join requests, drops its boot lease and removes it from the projection. The row is removed when nothing references it and tombstoned otherwise (`tombstoned: true`).

A retry after the delete returns `deleted: false`. Publishes `site.deleted`.

overview: The `system` group answers questions about the deployment itself. `whoami` and `version` are public and answer without a credential, which makes them a quick connectivity and credential check; `selfCheck` is a fleet administrator's health report. See [Observability](/docs/operations/observability).

methods.summary: Reports who is calling: `authenticated: false` without a credential, or the authenticated identity.
methods.description:
Reports who is calling: `authenticated: false` without a credential, or the authenticated identity.

Public; no IAM decision. When the call carries a credential, IAM authenticates it once and the answer holds the identity id and kind, the tenant, the session kind, whether the session used MFA, and the agent and delegation ids when present. The session id is never returned.

methods.summary: Returns the server's name, release version, API base path and the agent protocol versions it speaks.
methods.description:
Returns the server's name, release version, API base path and the agent protocol versions it speaks.

Public; no IAM decision and no input. The JoinService public keys appear only in the `.well-known/better-compute` document, not in this answer.

methods.summary: Runs the deployment's read-only health checks and returns the findings, with `ok` false when any finding is an `error`.
methods.description:
Runs the deployment's read-only health checks and returns the findings, with `ok` false when any finding is an `error`.

Decided as `compute:fleet:admin` on `compute-fleet/global`, which resolves only in the root tenant. The report covers the method catalog, applied migrations, the `btree_gist` extension, `compute_now()` against the database clock, the operations checks (overdue work, command sweeper lag, usage dead letters and backlog, gateway headroom, stale heartbeats, daemon protocol skew, expiring node certificates) and every module's own `selfCheck`. A failing check becomes an `error` finding rather than a failed call.

overview: Interactive access to an instance or a node through its gateway and daemon: exec, SSH, TCP or the serial console of an instance, or the console of a node. The server's tunnels module hosts this group when the deployment configures `tunnels` with an exec ticket issuer. See [Tunnels](/docs/guides/access/tunnels).

instanceId.description: Exec, ssh, tcp or the serial console of this instance; give exactly one of instanceId or nodeId

op.description: console for a node (a host shell); exec, ssh, tcp or console (its serial console) for an instance

port.description: tcp only: the port to reach

methods.summary: Issues a single-use exec ticket, valid for 60 seconds, for a tunnel to an instance or a node; returns the ticket, the tunnel id, the node and the `path` (`tunnels/<ticket>`, relative to the API base path) the caller then opens.
methods.description:
Issues a single-use exec ticket, valid for 60 seconds, for a tunnel to an instance or a node; returns the ticket, the tunnel id, the node and the `path` (`tunnels/<ticket>`, relative to the API base path) the caller then opens.

- Give exactly one of `instanceId` or `nodeId`. An instance takes `exec`, `ssh`, `tcp` (with a `port` from 1 to 65535) or `console` (its serial console: the daemon opens the domain's console from its runtime, never a host shell), decided with `compute:instances:exec` on `compute-instance/{instanceId}`. A node takes `console` only, decided with `compute:nodes:console` on `compute-node/{nodeId}`. Any other combination is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- Instance tunnels need a daemon that advertises `tunnel.instance-dial`: an older one would reach the host rather than the instance, so the call is `UNSUPPORTED` with `details.reason: 'daemon-capability'`; upgrade the daemon.
- A sandbox's instance, or a warm one waiting for a sandbox, takes no tunnels: `INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: 'sandbox-managed'`; `sandboxes.exec` is its only way in.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the instance is not the tenant's or is still a draft, or the node is outside the tenant's view. `UNSUPPORTED` for a provider instance, which has no node agent to tunnel through.
- `INVALID_STATE` when the instance is not `running` or its node is not connected to a gateway.
- `RATE_LIMITED` (with `retryAfterMs`) beyond the per-identity limit of each API replica, 10 tunnels per minute by default.
- Emits `tunnel.issued`.

overview: The hourly usage windows compute meters per allocation and hands to Better IAM billing, as the tenant can read them. Both methods decide `compute:usage:read` on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`, or on `compute-project/{projectId}` when the call names a project, since windows carry their project as a tag. See [Billing and usage](/docs/guides/iam/billing-and-usage).

methods.summary: Lists the tenant's usage windows ordered by window start, optionally for one project, one meter and a time range; returns a page with a cursor.
methods.description:
Lists the tenant's usage windows ordered by window start, optionally for one project, one meter and a time range; returns a page with a cursor.

- Each window carries its billing idempotency key (`cmp:<allocationId>:<windowStartMs>`), meter, quantity, bounds and tags, and, once the usage sink has handed it to IAM billing, `recordedAt` and the `outcome` (`recorded`, `duplicate`, `reattributed` or `dead-lettered`).
- `from` and `to` (epoch milliseconds) select windows that end after `from` and start before `to`; `to` not after `from` is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- `limit` is at most 500 (100 by default). A cursor this method did not return is `INVALID_INPUT`.

methods.summary: Exports every usage window of a time range as CSV (the default) or JSON Lines, with the window count and the summed quantity per meter.
methods.description:
Exports every usage window of a time range as CSV (the default) or JSON Lines, with the window count and the summed quantity per meter.

- `from` and `to` are required, and the range is at most 93 days; `to` not after `from`, or a longer range, is `INVALID_INPUT`.
- One export returns at most 50,000 windows; when more match, `truncated` is `true` and the range or meter should be narrowed.
- CSV has a header row and ISO 8601 timestamps; JSON Lines has one window object per line.

overview: Per-tenant subscriptions that POST every matching committed event to an HTTPS endpoint, signed with a secret only the tenant and Better Compute know, with at-least-once delivery, retries with backoff, dead letters and redelivery. The events module hosts this group, and every method decides `compute:webhooks:manage` on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`. See [Webhooks](/docs/guides/events/webhooks).

methods.summary: Creates an active webhook for a URL and 1 to 20 event type patterns; returns the webhook and its signing secret, which is shown this once.
methods.description:
Creates an active webhook for a URL and 1 to 20 event type patterns; returns the webhook and its signing secret, which is shown this once.

- A pattern is an exact event type, a family such as `reservation.*`, or `*`; a pattern that matches nothing in the event catalog is `INVALID_INPUT` (see `eventTypes`), unless the deployment is configured to accept any pattern.
- The URL must be absolute, use `https`, carry no credentials and not point at a private, loopback or other non-public address; otherwise `INVALID_INPUT`.
- A tenant has at most 20 webhooks by default; one more is `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`.
- The webhook receives events committed after it was created; earlier history is not replayed. The method takes no idempotency key, so a retry creates a second webhook.

methods.summary: Lists the tenant's webhooks, oldest first, without their secrets.
methods.description: Lists the tenant's webhooks, oldest first, without their secrets.

methods.summary: Returns one webhook of the tenant by id, without its secret.
methods.description:
Returns one webhook of the tenant by id, without its secret.

`NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Changes a webhook's URL, event patterns, description or `active` flag and increments its version; returns the webhook.
methods.description:
Changes a webhook's URL, event patterns, description or `active` flag and increments its version; returns the webhook.

- URL and patterns are checked as in `create` (`INVALID_INPUT`).
- Setting `active` to `false` pauses the webhook and cancels its pending deliveries.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Replaces a webhook's signing secret with a new one; returns the webhook and the new secret, shown this once.
methods.description:
Replaces a webhook's signing secret with a new one; returns the webhook and the new secret, shown this once.

- With `keepPreviousSeconds` (0 to 86,400, default 0), the old secret keeps signing deliveries alongside the new one until then, so receivers can switch without rejecting any; with 0 the old secret stops at once.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Deletes a webhook together with its delivery queue and history; returns `deleted: true`.
methods.description:
Deletes a webhook together with its delivery queue and history; returns `deleted: true`.

`NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Queues a `webhook.ping` delivery to the webhook, due now; returns the delivery.
methods.description:
Queues a `webhook.ping` delivery to the webhook, due now; returns the delivery.

The ping is a delivery only: it is not written to the outbox, so `events.list` does not show it. A ping to a paused webhook is cancelled when the delivery worker picks it up. `NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Lists a webhook's deliveries newest first, optionally filtered by `state` (`pending`, `delivered`, `dead` or `cancelled`), with attempts, the next attempt time and the last status or error.
methods.description:
Lists a webhook's deliveries newest first, optionally filtered by `state` (`pending`, `delivered`, `dead` or `cancelled`), with attempts, the next attempt time and the last status or error.

`limit` is at most 200 (50 by default). `NOT_FOUND` when the webhook is not the tenant's.

methods.summary: Puts a delivery back in the queue, due now, with its attempt count reset; returns the delivery.
methods.description:
Puts a delivery back in the queue, due now, with its attempt count reset; returns the delivery.

- Meant for `dead`, `cancelled` or `delivered` deliveries, for example once a failing endpoint is fixed.
- The delivery keeps its id, so the `X-Better-Compute-Delivery` header carries the same value as before.
- `NOT_FOUND` when the delivery is not the tenant's or its webhook is paused.

methods.summary: Returns the event catalog that webhook patterns are checked against: the built-in event families plus any plugin families the deployment configured, each with its type, subject, publishing module and description.
methods.description:
Returns the event catalog that webhook patterns are checked against: the built-in event families plus any plugin families the deployment configured, each with its type, subject, publishing module and description.

Decided like the rest of the group, with `compute:webhooks:manage` on `compute-tenant/{tenantId}`. The method comes from the events module and is not in core's API catalog, so it has no phase.

overview: The workflows group reads the provisioning workflows of a node and lets an operator abort, retry, pause or resume one. Workflows are started by other modules, such as metal for each workflow-driven provision state, not through this group. Every method is decided on the node (`compute-node`): reads as `compute:workflows:read`, the others as `compute:workflows:manage`. See [Provisioning workflows](/docs/guides/bare-metal/workflows).

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

methods.summary: Returns one workflow of the node with all its steps, including each step's phase, state, attempt, command, deadline, result and error.
methods.description:
Returns one workflow of the node with all its steps, including each step's phase, state, attempt, command, deadline, result and error.

`NOT_FOUND` unless the workflow belongs to the tenant and the node.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

cursor.description: The cursor of the previous page

methods.summary: Returns a page of the node's workflows with their steps, newest first.
methods.description:
Returns a page of the node's workflows with their steps, newest first.

`limit` defaults to 20 and is at most 100; pass the returned `cursor` to read the next page.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

methods.summary: Cancels a workflow: pending steps are cancelled, the in-flight step's command is cancelled, and the cleanup phase runs before the workflow ends `cancelled`.
methods.description:
Cancels a workflow: pending steps are cancelled, the in-flight step's command is cancelled, and the cleanup phase runs before the workflow ends `cancelled`.

- A `pending` or `failed` workflow is cancelled at once, with no cleanup, and publishes `workflow.cancelled`.
- Aborting a workflow that is already cancelled or cancelling does nothing; aborting a succeeded one is `INVALID_STATE`.
- The optional `reason` (at most 512 characters) is recorded in the workflow's error.

Aborting a workflow that metal owns fails the node; steer metal nodes with `metal.abort` and `metal.recover` instead.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

fromStep.description: The step id to start from (default: the first main step that did not succeed)

methods.summary: Runs a failed workflow again from `fromStep`, by default the first main step that did not succeed; that step and every later main step return to `pending` with the next attempt number, and on-failure and cleanup steps are re-armed.
methods.description:
Runs a failed workflow again from `fromStep`, by default the first main step that did not succeed; that step and every later main step return to `pending` with the next attempt number, and on-failure and cleanup steps are re-armed.

- `INVALID_STATE` unless the workflow is `failed`.
- `INVALID_INPUT` when `fromStep` is not a main step, or when every main step succeeded.
- `CONFLICT` when the node has another active workflow.

Publishes `workflow.retried` with the `fromStep`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

methods.summary: Pauses a running workflow: the step in flight finishes, but no further step starts until `resume`.
methods.description:
Pauses a running workflow: the step in flight finishes, but no further step starts until `resume`.

`INVALID_STATE` when the workflow is not `running`, or when it is in its cleanup phase after a failure or abort. Publishes `workflow.paused`.

tenantId.description: The tenant the call acts in

nodeId.description: The node the workflow runs on

methods.summary: Puts a paused workflow back to `running` and queues it to continue with its next step.
methods.description:
Puts a paused workflow back to `running` and queues it to continue with its next step.

`INVALID_STATE` when the workflow is not `paused`. Publishes `workflow.resumed`.
